visual_brief: Taipei 101 has a blue-green glass exterior, eight stacked outward-flaring pagoda-like sections, circular medallions near its lower shaft and a narrow tiered crown ending in a long spire. It dominates Taipei’s Xinyi district; Elephant Mountain and nearby hill viewpoints give the classic skyline view, while more distant street viewpoints show its facade. Do not confuse it with the nearby rectangular Taipei Nan Shan Plaza, Shin Kong Life Tower or Kaohsiung’s forked 85 Sky Tower. The supplied ref.jpg is a Taipei 101 logo, so photographic identity was checked against the article and identified source photographs.
notes: Six distinct photographs retained and visually checked; all exceed 2400 px on the long side. Recommended c1 for a portrait crop, or c2 for a native portrait composition. Ground-level obstructions are disclosed individually. All originals are from Pexels; no reference file was reused.
